payload.text: A solid cylinder rolls without slipping down a vertical drop h from rest.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Predict how the observable changes when the defining scale parameter is doubled, and justify the prediction quantitatively.

criteria.description: Doubling the drop height h increases the speed by a factor of √2 (not 2), since v = sqrt(4gh/3) is proportional to sqrt(h); the new speed equals √2 times the original speed.
required_evidence: speed is proportional to the square root of the drop height
doubling h multiplies v by √2, not by 2
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
criteria.minimum_fix: To earn this point, explicitly show speed is proportional to the square root of the drop height; doubling h multiplies v by √2, not by 2.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why combining translational and rotational kinetic energy terms, under the assumption that the cylinder rolls without slipping, justifies the derived speed at the bottom of the drop.

criteria.description: Correctly cites conservation of energy combining translational and rotational kinetic energy as the governing principle and states that rolling without slipping means no energy is lost to friction.
required_evidence: translational and rotational kinetic energy combined
no frictional energy loss while rolling
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
criteria.minimum_fix: To earn this point, explicitly show translational and rotational kinetic energy combined; no frictional energy loss while rolling.
